item.title: Kroger names former Walmart executive as new CEO
item.description: Kroger has named a former Walmart executive as its new chief executive officer, nearly a year after its previous CEO abruptly resigned.

item.title: Farmers & Merchants Bank hires UA grad for agriculture role
item.description: Farmers & Merchants Bank announces a new Ag Business Development Manager, who happens to be a University of Arkansas graduate.

item.title: Drug busts at several Logan County homes net 5 arrests
item.description: The Logan County Sheriff's Office said that a drug bust at multiple homes in the county last week netted five arrests.

item.title: Senator urges SEC action against Fayetteville company over alleged fake 'tribal tax credits'
item.description: Senator Ron Wyden (D– Oregon), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Committee, has formally called on the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to revoke the registration of Fayetteville-based White River Energy Corp. (ticker: WTRV), citing alleged investor fraud and repeated violations of federal securities laws.

item.title: Fisher stakes claim for spot in Arkansas pitching rotation
item.description: Fisher is 9-1 in his career for th Diamond Hogs

item.title: 2026 NWS storm-spotting classes in Northwest Arkansas
item.description: FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — The National Weather Service (NWS) in Tulsa is hosting storm spotter training sessions across northwest Arkansas between February and March.

item.title: Land trust protects 692 acres in Beaver Lake watershed with EPA grant
item.description: The Northwest Arkansas Land Trust (NWALT) has completed a three-year, EPA-funded conservation project that permanently protects 692 acres in the Beaver Lake Watershed.

item.title: Greenland School District asking for community support for millage increase
item.description: Greenland School District is asking its community to vote for a proposed millage increase on March 3, stating the money is needed for necessary improvements across the district.

item.title: LIVESTREAM: Fayetteville's State of the City address
item.description: KNWA/FOX24 is livestreaming the 2026 State of the City address on its website Feb. 10 from the Fayetteville Town Center, following the City Council’s agenda session.
